brief: Midterm election clarity drove a broad market rally: large- and small-cap equities rose and the VIX fell 20% as oil prices dropped on rising pressure to end the Iran conflict, while chip stocks sold off on anticipated data-center scrutiny. UBS frames the reaction as a relief rally predicated on lower oil, which also eased Treasury yields, raised the odds the Fed holds rates steady in January, and tightened credit spreads. Looking ahead, UBS argues gridlock under a Democratic Congress is broadly stable for markets, citing the Clinton-era precedent of negotiation during divided government, but says structural fiscal issues, a FY2026 deficit near 6.2% of GDP, keep longer-term rates elevated, and that reducing tariffs would widen the deficit further. Senate confirmation of Fed nominees under a Democrat-led chamber better protects Fed independence. Separately, Democratic campaigns against AI infrastructure and 40 anti-AI ballot measures widened hyperscaler credit spreads and triggered a chipmaker selloff, while cloud-capacity owners rallied; UBS expects state-level data-center regulation and higher electricity costs. M&A stays strong on mega-deals despite limited Democratic antitrust control.
